question: Why did Mike Godwin first spread his rule about Nazi comparisons across Usenet groups?
answer: As a deliberate experiment in spreading an idea. From 1990 Godwin, a lawyer, posted his rule, that a long online argument will sooner or later compare someone to Hitler, to make careless comparisons look foolish. He called it a counter-meme and described the test in Wired in October 1994. Others soon cited it unprompted.
move: An idea spreads furthest when it is short enough to quote.
reference: Mike Godwin, Meme, Counter-meme, Wired, issue 2.10, October 1994
